name: Differential Geometry

papers.title: Nonlocal approximation of stable minimal surfaces with prescribed number of connected components
papers.abstract: We show that every strictly stable classical minimal hypersurface in a Euclidean ball can be approximated, for $s$ sufficiently close to $1$, by a stable $s$-minimal surface in a smaller ball. We also give an explicit lower bound on the size of the interval of admissible values of $s$. As a consequence, we construct stable nonlocal minimal surfaces with an arbitrarily large number $k$ of connected components in a bounded region, under the quantitative condition $k \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{1-s}}$, attaining an optimal result (at least in dimensions $2$ and $3$). As part of the proof of our main result, we obtain an auxiliary result of independent interest, providing quantitative estimates for foliations of constant mean curvature embedded hypersurfaces near a stable minimal surface. The resulting foliation supplies nonlocal barriers thanks to known results of uniform convergence of the nonlocal mean curvature to the classical one when $s \to 1$.

papers.title: The Whitney sphere and tori as self-shrinkers
papers.abstract: We prove that the Whitney sphere in $\C^n$ is a self-shrinker for the Hamiltonian gradient flow of volume. We construct an explicit family of Lagrangian self-shrinking tori in $\C^2$ containing infinitely many pairwise noncongruent examples. We also characterize closed connected Lagrangian immersions whose Legendrian lifts lie in a Kor\'anyi sphere by showing that, up to scaling and a unitary transformation, they factor through the Whitney immersion via a diffeomorphism for $n\geq2$ and a finite covering for $n=1$.

papers.title: Geometry and Analysis of Spinor Valued Forms
papers.abstract: We study spinor valued differential forms, that is, sections of the bundles $\mathcal{S}_p=\mathcal{S}\otimes\Lambda_p\otimes L$ of spinor valued $p$-forms twisted by a $U(1)$ line bundle $L$, on compact even-dimensional Riemannian spin (or $\mathrm{Spin}^\mathbb{C}$) manifolds. We develop the algebra of spinor valued forms: the chirality, grading and duality involutions, the bilinear tensors built from spinor valued forms and the Fierz-type identities they satisfy, and the action of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ generated by Clifford multiplication and contraction, which we use to decompose the space of spinor valued forms into irreducible components and to construct an adapted orthonormal basis. We introduce the twisted exterior derivative and coderivative, the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators and, more generally, the natural first-order operators on spinor valued forms, as well as the twisted Hodge and signature operators, and derive their conformal transformation laws. We obtain the Weitzenb\"ock formulas for the twisted de Rham and Dirac Laplacians, express the curvature terms through the Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, the curvature of $L$ and the bilinear tensors of the spinor valued forms, and derive vanishing theorems, heat trace invariants and index formulas. Finally, in four dimensions we use these Weitzenb\"ock formulas to construct non-negative functionals whose absolute minima define two generalizations of the Seiberg--Witten monopole equations to right spinor valued $p$-forms, one based on the Dirac operator and one on the twisted de Rham Laplacian, and discuss the resulting integrability conditions.

papers.title: Equivariant cohomology of stacky Lie group actions
papers.abstract: In this work we introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie groupoids and differentiable stacks. For Lie groupoids equipped with a strict action of a Lie 2-group, we define the corresponding equivariant cohomology via the Borel model and establish its Morita invariance. We also construct a simplicial Cartan model and prove that, under standard compactness assumptions, it recovers the equivariant cohomology defined via the Borel model. In the framework of stacky Lie group actions, we show that if a connected and \'etale stacky Lie group acts on a differentiable stack admitting an equivariant atlas, then the stacky action admits a strict presentation by a Lie 2-group action. Furthermore, we prove that different choices of equivariant atlases yield equivariantly Morita equivalent presenting actions, giving rise to a well-defined notion of equivariant cohomology for differentiable stacks. As an application, we compute the equivariant cohomology of toric symplectic stacks.

papers.title: Reeb stability for singular Riemannian foliations
papers.abstract: We prove a global Reeb stability theorem for singular Riemannian foliations on compact connected manifolds using the semi-local model developed by Alexandrino et al. We show that all leaves are compact if and only if the foliation is infinitesimally closed, and there exists a compact leaf with a linear holonomy groupoid which is proper at that leaf. These conditions are also equivalent to the existence of a smooth map to a Euclidean space whose fibers are exactly the leaves. The proof combines a local criterion for strong stability with compact transverse leaves, Molino's structural theory, and polynomial descriptions of local leaf spaces. Around a closed leaf, we show that the linear holonomy groupoid realizes the original foliation precisely when the infinitesimal foliation is homogeneous. When the infinitesimal foliation is closed, properness of this groupoid yields an associated-bundle model whose compact structure group is its isotropy group. We also characterize the existence, near a compact leaf, of a Hausdorff model Lie groupoid which is proper at that leaf. As an application, we obtain stability results for maps whose connected fiber components form singular Riemannian foliations. We compare linear holonomy with Fernandes's reduced Lie algebroid holonomy and with formal outer holonomy. Finally, we prove that, for every infinitesimally closed singular Riemannian foliation, the compactly supported tangent vector fields form a locally finitely generated involutive module inducing the original leaf partition.

papers.title: On the rigidity of generalized cylinders
papers.abstract: We prove pointed Gromov--Hausdorff rigidity of cylinders $N\times\mathbb R^d$ whenever $N$ is a compact Einstein manifold rigid as a Ricci shrinker.

papers.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite bubbles
papers.abstract: Let $k\geq 6$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $k$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with $\mathrm{Ric}_h > \lambda $. In this paper, we construct, for each given $\epsilon >0$, a sequence of $(k+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(X\times\mathbb{S}^2 ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_\epsilon ,d_\epsilon ) $ with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} > \lambda $, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_\epsilon ) \leq \epsilon $, and $X_\epsilon $ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. In particular, the sequence of Riemannian manifolds we construct have uniformly bounded topology, which improves the earlier examples of Hupp-Naber-Wang and Zhou.

papers.title: Total Curvature and Topology of Complete Euclidean Immersions: Heat Kernel and Boundary Morse Approaches
papers.abstract: Two mechanisms relate the scale-invariant integral of the second fundamental form to topology at infinity of a complete Euclidean immersion. The first retains the mean-curvature potential in the Michael--Simon Sobolev inequality, establishes an ultracontractive estimate for the semigroup generated by $\Delta+|H|^2$, and uses a vector-bundle Cwikel--Lieb--Rozenblum bound to estimate spaces of $L^2$-harmonic forms. Together with the theory of nonparabolic ends, this yields $e(M)\le 1+C_n\int_M|A|^n$ for arbitrary complete immersed $n$-manifolds, $n\ge3$. The second method, under the additional assumption of finitely many single-sheeted $C^2$-asymptotically planar graphical ends, uses a boundary Morse complex and the normal Gauss-map area formula to prove $\sum_j b_j(M;\F)+e(M)-2\le\TA(F)$. It supplies an explicit end coefficient and bounds ordinary Betti numbers. We provide proofs of both mechanisms, identify the exact role of their respective hypotheses, and discuss minimal and Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian specializations.

papers.title: Three-dimensional harmonic critical metrics for the Einstein-Hilbert functional and self-similar Ricci flows
papers.abstract: We address the three-dimensional harmonic analogue of Hilbert's variational problem: does criticality of the Einstein-Hilbert functional under volume-preserving Chen-Nagano variations force constant sectional curvature, and how is this rigidity related to Ricci flow and topology? Starting from the known characterization of compact harmonic critical metrics as gradient Ricci solitons, we use Ivey's classification to show that such metrics on closed three manifolds are precisely the space-form metrics, equivalently the stationary metrics of the volume-normalized Ricci flow. We also describe residual gauge one-forms, establish transversality of the Chen-Nagano gauge to infinitesimal diffeomorphism directions, and give explicit self-similar flows. The normalized Ricci-flow velocity is an admissible Chen-Nagano variation for n > = 3, and the smooth Poincar'e theorem admits an equivalent formulation in terms of the existence of harmonic critical metrics

papers.title: Smooth approximation of one-sided minimizing CMC hypersurfaces with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We consider a CMC hypersurface with an isolated singularity, given by the boundary of a set of finite perimeter, that minimizes the prescribed mean curvature functional on one side. If a varifold tangent at the singularity is a non--flat regular cone of multiplicity--1 that minimizes perimeter on the side occupied by the blow--up, then we show that, in a small neighborhood of the singular point, there exists a sequence of smooth CMC hypersurfaces, with the same prescribed mean curvature, that converges to the initial hypersurface. We also establish the full CMC variational equation and regularity for minimizers of a class of singular obstacle problems.

papers.title: Rigidity of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics at Isotropy Order $n-6$
papers.abstract: We classify linearly full, irreducible, totally unramified conformal minimal two-spheres of constant Gaussian curvature in the real Grassmannian $G(2,n;\mathbb R)$, or equivalently in the complex hyperquadric $Q_{n-2}$, whose finite isotropy order is $n-6$, where $n\geq7$. We remove the additional polynomiality assumption on a Frenet norm in the earlier classification of Li and Jiao. An exterior-product norm identity reduces the problem to the multiplicity of the irreducible polynomial $1+zw$; a further divisibility argument handles the boundary dimension $n=7$, including isotropy order one. The dimension $n$ is necessarily odd, and the immersion is congruent, after a conformal reparametrization, to the second member of a Veronese sequence with its prescribed real structure. Its curvature is $2/(5n-13)$ in the Grassmannian normalization. An explicit model in $Q_5$ illustrates the boundary case and its harmonic sequence.

papers.title: Veronese Classification of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics
papers.abstract: We prove that every linearly full, irreducible conformal minimal immersion of constant Gaussian curvature and finite isotropy order from the two-sphere into a complex hyperquadric comes from a member of a Veronese sequence. The result holds at every finite isotropy order, without an unramifiedness or additional Frenet-norm polynomiality assumption. Both the associated projective harmonic sequence and the target harmonic sequence are totally unramified as consequences. If the replacement depth is \(\ell\) and the holomorphic seed spans \(\mathbb{CP}^m\), the curvature is \(K=2/((2\ell+1)m-2\ell^2)\) in the Grassmannian normalization. Real Gram data characterize the admissible embeddings and give an algebraic converse. The proof uses holomorphic Pfaffian norm identities, degree estimates that retain all ramification divisors, and a valuation argument that identifies the retained lines with seed Frenet lines.

papers.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on vector bundles II: the non-simple case
papers.abstract: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system on the space of Fubini-Study metrics on a polarized compact K\"ahler manifold. Sano proved that if there exists a balanced metric for the polarization, then this dynamical system always converges to the balanced metric provided that the automorphism group is discrete (\cite{S}). In \cite{DKLR}, Douglas, et.\ al., conjecture that the same holds in the case of vector bundles. In \cite{Se}, we proved their conjecture under the assumption that the bundle is simple. In this note, we remove the simplicity assumption. The main tool is Thompson's metric on the space of Hermitian inner products on the space of holomorphic sections, with respect to which the generalized $T$-operator is non-expanding.

papers.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
papers.abstract: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $\rho_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $\rho_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).

papers.title: Integrability and closed spacelike extremals of conformal arclength in the Einstein universe
papers.abstract: We study the conformal arclength functional for nondegenerate spacelike curves in the three-dimensional Einstein universe and classify its closed extremals up to conformal equivalence. We show that the extremals are projections of trajectories of a generically noncommutatively integrable Reeb flow. For extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants, closedness forces negative helicity and regular elliptic momentum. We prove that the restricted moment map over the corresponding invariant region defines a nontrivial principal $\mathbb T^3$-bundle, and construct explicit local trivializations that linearize the Reeb flow. This yields explicit parametrizations in terms of elliptic functions and integrals. We prove that the associated period map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto a bounded, convex planar domain whose rational points parametrize the conformal equivalence classes of closed extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants. We conclude with a study of the global geometry of closed extremals.

papers.title: The exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation
papers.abstract: We solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation of minimal type over the complementary of domains satisfying an interior sphere condition, and investigate some related problems. Namely, by linearizing the Weingarten equation, we give an asymptotic expansion for exterior solutions and we completely identify which classes of Weingarten minimal ends satisfy a maximum principle at infinity. Building on the previous results, we study symmetries of the solutions and questions related to the uniqueness of the solutions.

papers.title: Existence of complete singular solutions of the Yamabe equation at prescribed points
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be smooth, connected and closed, with $n\ge3$, and let $P$ be a prescribed nonempty finite set. We characterize the conformal classes $[g]$ that admit a complete metric of positive constant scalar curvature on $M\setminus P$. Such a metric exists precisely when $Y(M,[g])>0$ and either $[g]$ is nonround or $|P|\ge2$. In a nonround positive conformal class, the metrics can be chosen with Fowler asymptotics and arbitrary fixed ratios of their small asymptotic neck sizes. As the neck sizes tend to zero, every sequence of these metrics has a subsequence converging smoothly away from the punctures to a smooth Yamabe minimizing metric. The construction allows degenerate Yamabe minimizers and arbitrary curvature jets at the prescribed points. For nonempty closed singular sets $\Lambda\subset M$ with empty interior, we also announce the same existence criterion with the additional requirement that the Bessel capacity $C_{1+2/n,n/2}(\Lambda)$ vanish.

papers.title: Tian-Yau-type metrics from K3 divisors with ADE contractions
papers.abstract: We construct complete Ricci-flat K\"ahler metrics on the complement of a smooth anti-canonical K3 divisor in a compact K\"ahler threefold, assuming that the normal bundle of the divisor is nef and big. Such a metric exists in every K\"ahler class whose exceptional periods are positive. We use a generalized Gibbons-Hawking ansatz to construct an approximate model on the normal bundle. When the normal bundle contracts an ADE configuration, this model combines an expanding Ricci-flat orbifold K3 metric with ALE metrics whose exceptional periods remain fixed. After improving the model by a finite iteration and transferring it to the divisor complement, we apply the Tian-Yau-Hein existence theorem.

papers.title: Rigidity of submanifolds under extrinsic curvature pinching
papers.abstract: We investigate the rigidity of compact submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Riemannian manifolds whose curvature operator is bounded below by a nonnegative constant, under pointwise pinching conditions involving the second fundamental form and the mean curvature. In contrast to many earlier results, we allow equality in these conditions without imposing additional assumptions on the mean curvature or restricting the fundamental group of the submanifold. Allowing equality reveals geometric and topological phenomena excluded by strict pinching. We establish classification theorems in all dimensions $n\geq4$, describing the possible intrinsic geometries and topologies of such submanifolds. Our results also provide substantial information about the extrinsic geometry of the immersions, including precise conclusions concerning relative nullity, Dupin principal normals, and total geodesicity. As applications, we derive rigidity and sphere theorems for submanifolds of space forms and construct families of examples showing that the pinching conditions do not, in general, imply extrinsic rigidity. These results extend and refine several known rigidity theorems by providing a classification of the equality cases in a general ambient setting.

papers.title: Left-Invariant Kundt Structures on Almost Abelian Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We study left-invariant Kundt structures on almost abelian Lie groups. We establish algebraic existence criteria and characterize the admissible real Jordan forms according to the signature of the Abelian ideal. We then characterize the Kundt pairs defining pp-waves and plane waves in arbitrary dimension, with particular attention to recurrent and parallel null directions. Examples in dimension four illustrate both plane and non-plane pp-wave geometries.

papers.title: Time-optimal travel driven by two vector fields on a Riemannian manifold
papers.abstract: We study minimum-time travel on a Riemannian manifold $(M,h)$ for a kinematic model in which finitely many drift fields contribute additively to the velocity, after independent rescaling of their components parallel and orthogonal to a chosen unit direction $u$. The velocity is then $\mathcal Y_x(u)=(\eta(x)+h_x(\widehat Z_x,u))u+\widehat W_x$, $u\in UT_xM$, for two effective vector fields $\widehat Z$, $\widehat W$ and a self-propulsion speed $\eta\geq0$. Let $F$ be the gauge of the radial hull $\mathcal B_x=[0,1]\cdot\mathcal S_x$ of the velocity set $\mathcal S_x=\mathcal Y_x(UT_xM)$. Where $\eta>0$, we characterize when $F$ is a Finsler metric and give two-sided estimates and representation formulae for it; where $\eta=0$ and $\widehat Z\neq0$, we recover the Randers, Kropina and strong-wind regimes of Zermelo navigation. Examples include Matsumoto's slope metric, traction-modified slope models, and alternative models for wildfire propagation and microswimmer navigation. Since $F$ need not be a Finsler metric, we treat the minimum-time problem with tools from differential inclusions. For distinct endpoints, the inclusions defined by $\mathcal S_x$ and $\mathcal B_x$ give the same infimum travel time, and so does the convex hull of $\mathcal B_x$ under local controllability at the terminal point. When $F$ is finite, the infimum is attained if $(M,h)$ is complete, $\mathcal Y$ is bounded and each $\mathcal B_x$ is convex. When $F$ is a Finsler metric on $\{\eta>0\}$, the set $\{\eta=0\}$ cannot be reached from $\{\eta>0\}$ in finite time and, on $\{\eta>0\}$, the minimum time is the Finsler distance; if moreover $(M,h)$ is complete and $\eta$ is bounded, $F$ is forward and backward complete and the minimum time is attained by geodesics. We also compute the support Hamiltonian directly from the velocity law, for every $\eta\geq0$.

papers.title: Cosmological rigidity in $3$ spacetime dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. In the setting of the Bartnik Splitting Conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. Our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of Penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. Our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. In its proof, we make use of the local Kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.

papers.title: Sharp Barycentric Costs in Teichmuller Space
papers.abstract: The affine Beltrami fiber over a closed hyperbolic surface has a quadratic normal response whose least vertical $L^2$ energy equals the tangent norm dual to the hyperbolic cotangent supremum norm. We prove this calibration using a curvature identity and exact localized responses. Its strictness determines the energy measures of near-minimizers and, under an amplitude constraint, gives a positive excess with an explicit quadratic lower coefficient when the supporting differential has nondegenerate maxima. Pointwise Poincar'e barycenters of representatives in one fiber give a nonlinear realization: equal-weight pairs attain prescribed small outputs exactly, and their creation energy approaches the calibrated norm if and only if the output scale is negligible relative to the squared amplitude bound. Restoring the full local fiber graph has leading cost four times the squared Weil--Petersson norm. For degenerating surfaces, we identify the additive limit of the calibrated norm across persistent components and collar directions. The induced length metric completes to marked augmented Teichm"uller space and has distance $\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_i \ell_i + O((\sum_i \ell_i)^2)$ to a fixed pinching stratum. Systole-dependent estimates also yield exact nonlinear realizations along degenerating families.

papers.title: A singular Lawson cone minimizing the fractional perimeter in dimension seven
papers.abstract: We prove that the nonlocal Lawson cone constructed by Davila, del Pino, and Wei (J. Differential Geom. 2018) in $N=7$ minimizes the fractional perimeter for all sufficiently small orders $s$. Thus nonlocal minimal surfaces can have singularities already in dimension $7$. This contrasts both with the classical theory, where the first singular example occurs in dimension $8$ (Bombieri-De Giorgi-Giusti, Invent. Math. 1969), and with the fractional theory for orders $s$ close to $1$ (Caffarelli-Valdinoci, Adv. Math. 2013).

papers.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
papers.abstract: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

papers.title: On the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point for the Yamabe equation in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point of solutions to the Yamabe equation in every dimension $n\ge 25$. On every closed, connected, smooth $n$-dimensional manifold $M$ of positive Yamabe type and at any prescribed point $p\in M$, we construct a smooth metric $ \widehat g$ and a sequence of smooth positive solutions to the Yamabe equation blowing up at $p$, such that the first nonzero covariant derivative of the Weyl tensor at $p$ has any prescribed order $l$ satisfying $l\ge 6$ when $25\le n\le 29$, $l \ge 4$ when $30\le n\le 51$, and $l\ge 2$ when $n\ge 52$. Moreover, $|\nabla_{ \widehat g}^{l}W_{ \widehat g}|>0$ everywhere on $M$. Earlier constructions realize every strictly higher order as the first nonzero order, while the known Weyl vanishing results exclude every lower first nonzero order. Thus the endpoint cases $l=6,4,2$ were the only ones left open, and are settled here. In particular, the order-two examples show that the compactness criterion $|W|+|\nabla W|>0$ is sharp. At the endpoints, the construction arranges global and localized metric perturbations to interact at leading order in a limiting functional. For $l=2,4$, anisotropic polynomial ansatzes involving two orthogonal algebraic Weyl tensors remove a distinguished translation degeneracy and produce $C^1$-stable saddle points. For $l=6$, a different polynomial ansatz produces a nondegenerate local minimum. Higher prescribed orders are obtained by separating the perturbation that determines the limiting functional from the one that prescribes the Weyl derivative.

papers.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
papers.abstract: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact K\"ahler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.

papers.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $\Lambda>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrt{\Lambda}/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $\Lambda > 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $\Lambda>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

papers.title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
papers.abstract: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

papers.title: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
papers.abstract: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.
